title: PCENChar defines valid tag names as including Unicode characters BUT...which Unicode representation?

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
Currently:

> PCENChar ::=
>     "-" | "." | [0-9] | "_" | [a-z] | #xB7 | [#xC0-#xD6] | [#xD8-#xF6] | [#xF8-#x37D] | [#x37F-#x1FFF] | [#x200C-#x200D] | [#x203F-#x2040] | [#x2070-#x218F] | [#x2C00-#x2FEF] | [#x3001-#xD7FF] | [#xF900-#xFDCF] | [#xFDF0-#xFFFD] | [#x10000-#xEFFFF]

I'm okay with Unicode characters as long as I know how to clearly define them.  Except there are at least 3 base flavors of Unicode representations (UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32, with the latter two having byte order issues) and many other custom Unicode representations (HTML has at least 3 of its own).  If `Content-Type` is expected to declare which Unicode representation, then that's going to cause problems with parsing a generic document that may not know the `Content-Type` of the HTML.  If a BOM is expected/required, that would be problematic too.  Assuming UTF-8 is seemingly sane at first, and is probably the most widely supported Unicode representation, but that's just asking for worse trouble further down the road especially if there ends up being mixed character sets on the same page - how does someone create/edit HTML stored in multiple character sets in an IDE or other text editor?  That's a problem XML doesn't have but HTML would have.

At the very least, there needs to be one example attempting to demonstrate the use of the Unicode characters in the specified ranges.  (The Notes section briefly mentions <math-α> and <emotion-😍> but then Unicode isn't referenced ever again.  I don't count that comment as a valid example.)  The examples so far stick fairly strictly to a-z and hyphen even though the broader definition of PCENChar offers much more room for a variety of character-related shenanigans (e.g. abusing Unicode combining code points).

I feel like a first iteration of custom tag names (e.g. a CTN1) should only slightly expand the current definition for tag names and not try to be everything/rock the boat too much.  Personally, I'd save the crazy Unicode support bits and other odd characters like #B7 for a CTN2 if/when CTN1 works well enough and gets used fairly widely.  Taking away or changing something is much harder to do than adding something.  Unicode support also comes with its own caveats including security vulnerabilities.

I'm also slightly against having "." be included in the set of allowed characters as it requires escaping each dot in CSS.  That is, `my\.new\.tag.my-class { ... }` might work fine but is kind of ugly to look at.  CSS classes already allow for dots in class names (again, escaped), so I guess it's okay-ish for custom tag names.

> PCENChar ::=
>     "-" | "." | [0-9] | "_" | [a-z]

That's my recommendation (with the use of "." being looked dimly upon).  The first character has to be `a-z` anyway, which is kind of limiting if custom elements tag names were going for full Unicode support.  Also, there's Punycode (RFC3492) or a hacked up RFC1342 that could operate within that restricted character set - albeit, neither one being a particularly good option/solution.
